name: Professional services
description: Law firms, accountants, consultants, architects, agencies and advisers. Clients hire expertise they cannot judge, so the site sells trust: credentials, results and a clear first step.

goals.prompt: What should the website do for your firm? Name the one or two results that matter most.
goals.why: A professional site is judged by consultations booked from the right kind of client.

recommendation.statement: Get the right clients to book a first consultation
Show expertise and results that make a stranger trust the firm

goals.reason: The two jobs of a professional-services site.

audience.prompt: Who is your ideal client, and what problem is pushing them to look for help now? One per line; add if known: wants: ... | proof: ... | action: ... | from: ... | mood: ...
audience.why: The site speaks to that person's problem first and the firm's credentials second.

recommendation.segment: Business owners and individuals with a specific problem to solve
recommendation.need: Know the firm handles it, see proof, and understand the first step and the cost

audience.reason: A safe starting audience; research in P2 refines it.

heroMustHave: A headline that names the problem solved and for whom, not the firm's name alone
A phone number visible without scrolling on a phone, next to the primary action

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: Name the problem the firm solves, prove the firm can be trusted and lead the visitor to a consultation

pages.title: Services
pages.purpose: Explain each service by the client problem it solves, who it is for and what happens next

pages.title: About the Firm
pages.purpose: Show the firm's approach, history and values in plain words

pages.title: Our Team
pages.purpose: Introduce each partner and adviser with credentials and focus areas

pages.title: Contact
pages.purpose: Make the first step easy, with the booking form, phone, address and hours

pages.title: Results and Case Studies
pages.purpose: Prove expertise with anonymised case studies: the problem, what was done and the outcome

pages.title: How We Work
pages.purpose: Take away uncertainty by showing each step from first call to delivery

pages.title: Fees and Engagement
pages.purpose: Set expectations on cost and how the engagement works, without hiding behind 'it depends'

pages.title: Industries We Serve
pages.purpose: Show the sectors the firm knows, so a visitor sees their own business reflected

pages.title: Client Testimonials
pages.purpose: Let clients speak, with names and companies where they agree

pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions
pages.purpose: Answer the questions that stop a prospect from calling

pages.title: Insights
pages.purpose: Publish expert guidance that brings in clients searching for answers

pages.title: Resources
pages.purpose: Offer checklists and guides in exchange for a contact, to start relationships early

pages.title: Careers
pages.purpose: Attract talent with the culture, the work and the roles open

questions.prompt: List the services or practice areas you offer, most important first.
questions.why: The first leads the home page; each gets a section or page.

questions.prompt: Describe the client you most want more of: who they are and what they come to you for.
questions.why: The hero speaks to this person.
Prospects who cannot guess the cost often do not call.

options.label: A mix, depending on the work

questions.prompt: What happens in the first consultation, how long is it and does it cost anything?
questions.why: A clear first step lowers the barrier to booking.

questions.prompt: What proof can you show: results, well-known clients, publications or awards?
questions.why: Proof does the selling; only what you supply is used.

questions.prompt: May the site name clients and describe results, or must everything be anonymised?
questions.why: It decides how case studies are written.
questions.reason: The safe default for confidential work.

questions.prompt: Where are your offices, and do you serve clients remotely?
questions.why: It decides the local promise and the contact page.

questions.prompt: Which of these do you already have?
questions.why: Real portraits and a profile deck are what the site is built from.

options.label: A firm profile or capability deck

/: hero naming the problem solved, a proof line, the primary action and a phone number
the main services by client problem
proof: credentials, results or well-known clients
how the first consultation works in three steps
a closing consultation call to action
/team: a profile per partner with photograph, credentials and focus
/contact: a map when there is an office

contentNeeds: List of services with a short description of each
Case studies or results that may be shown
compliance: Never state results, rankings or credentials the client has not supplied with a source
Never promise outcomes; describe what the firm does, not what the client will win or save
Follow the profession's advertising rules: the client must confirm the wording of any claim

extras.note: A calendar link makes the first consultation a single step.
For architects and designers, the portfolio is the proof.
Rarely helps a trust-led firm; a short founder video can, if recorded by the client.
Only suits architecture and design firms with real models to show.
